clue.text: Mad Hatter cast with difficulty

indicators.note: something mad is crazed and disordered, so the letters of the next two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Casting the Mad Hatter for a production of Alice proved a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad Hatter' reads as Lewis Carroll's character, but 'Mad' is only the anagram signal for HATTER CAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something only by straining or stretching yourself means doing it with effort, barely managing.

clue.text: Got rid of soap actor finally — Den is murdered

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the word actor in front of it
murdered is used figuratively for mangling, so the letters of Den is get rearranged

explanation.surface: A soap actor's story ends with Den being killed off.
explanation.walkthrough: Den Watts was a famous EastEnders soap character, killed off on screen; 'murdered' scrambles DEN IS into INSED after R.
explanation.definitionFit: After washing you clear off the lather with clean water, which is exactly that act.

clue.text: Scrap job and leave, introducing learner as cover

parts.note: a scrap of fabric is a patch
a job is work

indicators.note: introducing means the learner is brought into the middle of the word for leave

parts.note: to leave is to quit
L is the learner driver's plate letter

explanation.surface: Someone abandons one job and takes on a trainee to stand in for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' and 'job' read as a phrase about quitting work, but they are nouns; 'introducing' slips the learner's L inside the word for leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed quilt sewn from many small fabric scraps is a covering for a bed.

clue.text: High time to get drink? It's unbelievable

parts.note: high means tall
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone claims it is high time for a drink and nobody believes them.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaggerated story too far-fetched to credit is the very thing nobody can believe.

clue.text: Animals launched in one stage of flight

indicators.note: launched means sent upward, which in a down clue turns the word for animals bottom to top

parts.note: pets are domestic animals

explanation.surface: Animals are sent up on one leg of a space flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests aircraft or rockets, but it is a flight of stairs; 'launched' sends PETS upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is made of single treads, each one a level you climb.

clue.text: In the middle of punt, eating chocolate bar

indicators.note: eating means the word for punt swallows the chocolate bar inside it

parts.note: a punt is a bet, a wager
Twix is a well-known brand of chocolate bar

explanation.surface: Someone in a punt on the river is munching a chocolate bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests the flat boat, but it is a gamble, BET; Twix is a UK and US chocolate bar.
explanation.definitionFit: This old preposition means between, so placed amid two things.

clue.text: What's British local leader in control over?

definitions.text: What's British local leader in control over?

indicators.note: over signals that the whole assembled string is turned round
in places the local leader inside the word for control

parts.note: to hold sway is to have control

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word local

explanation.surface: A question about what a British town council chief has authority over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside SWAY, B follows, and 'over' turns SWALYB round.
explanation.definitionFit: Local regulations made by a council are precisely what a town's leadership controls.

clue.text: Apeman that could prevent site access?

explanation.surface: An early human ancestor is blamed for a website failing to load.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the supposed evolutionary intermediate between apes and humans; the second imagines a broken hyperlink stopping you reaching a web page.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings: the hypothetical fossil bridging apes and humans, and an absent web hyperlink that would leave a page unreachable.

clue.text: Fitting connecting plug and other terminals

definitions.text: Fitting connecting plug and other terminals

indicators.note: connecting means the word for fitting is placed between the other two pieces, joining them

parts.note: a plug is an advertisement, an ad

indicators.note: terminals means the first and last letters of the word other

parts.note: fitting means apt, suitable

explanation.surface: An electrical part that joins a plug to some other socket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminals' takes the first and last letters of 'other'; 'connecting' sets the word for fitting between the advert and those letters, so the pieces join just as the device does.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a device links one kind of electrical plug to a socket of another type.

clue.text: Does paper over cracked centre of plaster, sized

indicators.note: cracked means broken up, so the central letters picked out are jumbled
centre of takes the middle six letters of the twelve-letter phrase plaster sized, three dropped at each end

explanation.surface: A decorator papers over a crack in the middle of some sized plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface is about wallpapering, but 'Does paper over' means sits an exam again; 'centre of' spans both words, giving STERSI, which 'cracked' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Retaking an examination you failed is sitting the same test a second time.

clue.text: Is getting out of practice … on the other hand, has desire

indicators.note: on the other hand means switch hands, so right becomes left and the R changes to an L

parts.note: a skill that is getting out of practice rusts

explanation.surface: Someone losing their touch nevertheless still wants it.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L are the usual abbreviations for right and left; 'on the other hand' swaps one for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To crave or long for something strongly is to feel desire for it.

clue.text: Runs off around 50 duck fillets

indicators.note: around means the word for runs off goes round the other letters

parts.note: runs off means escapes
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: Someone flees around fifty ducks destined for the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the bird to go with 'fillets', but it is a cricket score of zero, O.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin boneless slices of meat, often veal, are the dish meant here.

clue.text: I'm amazed to comprehend awful drivel making outlook on life

indicators.note: to comprehend means to take in, so the exclamation encloses the other letters

parts.note: wow is an exclamation of amazement

indicators.note: awful signals the letters of drivel are in a terrible mess

explanation.surface: Someone astonished at grasping the nonsense that forms another's philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to comprehend' puts RLDVIE, the anagram of DRIVEL signalled by 'awful', inside the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's overall philosophy or perspective is how they view everything around them.

clue.text: A second series of games giving advantage

parts.note: in tennis a set is a series of games

explanation.surface: A tennis player gains the upper hand by winning the second set.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useful or valuable that helps you is a benefit in your favour.

clue.text: A French tart picked up in Swiss town for public health

indicators.note: in signals the earlier pieces sit inside the Swiss town

parts.note: Sion is a town in Switzerland, capital of the Valais

indicators.note: picked up means lifted, which in a down clue turns the word bottom to top

parts.note: tarte Tatin is the French upside-down apple tart

explanation.surface: A tart bought in Switzerland raises concerns over hygiene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns the tart's name upward in this down entry, giving NITAT; 'in' then places A and that inside the Swiss town. Tarte Tatin is an upside-down apple tart.
explanation.definitionFit: Drains, sewerage and clean water provision are the measures that protect community hygiene.

clue.text: Ashes perhaps provide spur for one who's handy with the willow?

definitions.text: one who's handy with the willow?

parts.note: ashes are an example of trees, the perhaps flagging the example
to provide a spur is to urge on

explanation.surface: Cricket's Ashes series spurs on a batsman good with a willow bat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the England-Australia cricket series and cricket bats are made of willow, so the whole clue pretends to be about batting.
explanation.definitionFit: An arborist prunes and tends trees, willow among them, so is skilled with that wood in another sense.

clue.text: Barrier missing both ends — pest to intrude

indicators.note: missing both ends means the word for barrier loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
a roach (cockroach) is a pest

explanation.surface: With the fence gone at both ends, vermin get in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing both ends' cuts F and E from FENCE, leaving ENC.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass gradually on someone's territory or rights is to intrude on them.

clue.text: Felt good, getting husband in to do housework

indicators.note: in places the husband inside the phrase for felt good

parts.note: if you felt good you were up, in high spirits

explanation.surface: Someone was pleased to get their husband doing the chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is only a link; 'in' puts the husband inside a phrase meaning felt good, and 'housework' tempts you towards cleaning rather than dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaning the dishes after a meal is a typical domestic chore.

clue.text: Every other word in Noel's show is a distressing experience

parts.words: Every other word in Noel's show
parts.note: Noel Edmonds hosted the TV game show Deal or No Deal; its second and fourth words are taken

parts.words: Every other word in Noel's show
parts.note: Noel Edmonds hosted the TV game show Deal or No Deal; its second and fourth words are taken

explanation.surface: Someone finds Noel's show unbearable, word after word.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal or No Deal was a British TV game show hosted by Noel Edmonds; taking every other word gives the two words that make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful trial or harrowing time is a terrible experience to live through.

clue.text: Guarantee on wine bottles Department of Health provided for this purpose

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so the wine guarantee encloses the department

parts.note: AOC, appellation d'origine controlee, is the French wine quality guarantee
DH is the abbreviation for the Department of Health

explanation.surface: The health department issues a guarantee covering wine bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like a noun about wine but is the verb of containment.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase meaning arranged specially, just for the particular need at hand.

clue.text: Mercilessness of Japanese theatre district

parts.note: No (Noh) is classical Japanese theatre
a quarter is a district of a town

explanation.surface: Cruelty in a Japanese theatre district.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing no clemency to a defeated enemy is refusing them mercy, giving none.

clue.text: Greek war leader controlling military intelligence bodies

indicators.note: controlling means holding, so the war god's name surrounds the intelligence letters

parts.note: Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: A Greek warlord directs his intelligence service.
explanation.definitionFit: Large organised groups of soldiers are bodies of troops.

clue.text: Holding election is hard, getting ways to attract attention for the masses

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the attention calls go round the election

parts.note: oi is a call to attract attention, and the plural gives two of them
a poll is an election

explanation.surface: Holding a vote is difficult when shouting is the only way to get noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' puts the election between two shouts of 'oi' (the plural 'ways' supplies two), after the pencil-hardness letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek phrase used in English for ordinary common people, the populace.

clue.text: I put off odd characters in a careless manner

indicators.note: odd characters means only the first, third and fifth letters of the word for put off are kept

parts.note: to put off is to delay

explanation.surface: Someone is turned off by strange people behaving carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd characters' looks like eccentric people, but it keeps D, L, Y, the odd-numbered letters of DELAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something lazily or without purpose is acting in a careless, aimless way.

clue.text: Joint episcopal head may come under this

definitions.text: episcopal head may come under this

explanation.surface: A woodworker's joint and a bishop's headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a carpentry joint at a 45-degree angle; the second is a bishop's tall pointed hat, which his head goes under.
explanation.definitionFit: Both: a corner joint in woodwork with angled ends, and the tall headdress a bishop wears.

clue.text: One having big bill in place that's falling apart

indicators.note: falling apart means breaking up, so the letters of in place are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with a huge debt lives in a home that is crumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big bill' suggests a large invoice, but it is a bird's beak.
explanation.definitionFit: This water bird is known for its huge beak with a pouch below it.

clue.text: Non-kosher ingredient for cooking plant

parts.note: tref is the Yiddish word for non-kosher food
oil is a cooking ingredient

explanation.surface: A forbidden ingredient goes into a cooked dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Clover and similar three-leaved species are this kind of plant.
